source.brief: iQmethod financial metric definitions and formulas.
source.description: Standardised BofA methodology table for consistent cross-company financial analysis in the internet coverage cluster.

properties.table_content:
Business Performance                Numerator                                                                  Denominator
Return On Capital Employed          NOPAT = (EBIT + Interest Income) (1 - Tax Rate) + Goodwill Amortization    Total Assets - Current Liabilities + ST Debt + Accumulated Goodwill 
                                                                                                               Amortization 
Return On Equity                    Net Income                                                                 Shareholders' Equity 
Operating Margin                    Operating Profit                                                           Sales 
Earnings Growth                     Expected 5 Year CAGR From Latest Actual                                    N/A 
Free Cash Flow                      Cash Flow From Operations - Total Capex                                    N/A
properties.key_insight: iQmethod provides transparent, standardised formulas for measuring business performance across Alphabet and sector peers.

| 2020 | -150 to +400 | Strong positive spikes, particularly early in the year, then mixed. |
| 2021 | -200 to +400 | Significant positive spikes, some notable outflows. |

| Category | Sub-category | Amount ($bn) | Cost per MW |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total Capex 2025-2028 | | $2,890 | N/A |
| Global Build Costs | Total | $1,296 | N/A |
| Global Build Costs | US | $754 | ~$11mm/MW |
| Global Build Costs | APAC | $101 | ~$8mm/MW |
| Global Build Costs | Europe | $117 | ~$12mm/MW |
| Global Build Costs | ROW | $324 | ~$10mm/MW |
| Total Hardware Costs | Total | $1,594 | N/A |

| Total Hardware Costs | non-AI Hardware | $175 | ~$6.5mm/MW |
properties.key_insight: Global data center capex of $2.89 trillion for 2025-2028 split into $1.296 trillion build costs and $1.594 trillion hardware costs, with US build costs at $754 billion and AI hardware costs at $1.419 trillion.

| 2018 | ($300) to $400                              | Relatively contained flows. |
| 2019 | ($200) to $500                              | Mostly net buying. |
| 2020 | ($1,000) to $800                            | Sharp rebound in buying after deep early outflows. |

source.name: Table T1 – Future GW-scale data center architecture
source.brief: Hierarchical data center power delivery architecture featuring voltage step-down and advanced materials.
source.description: Outlines multi-stage power conversion from MV AC to serverboard core, leveraging SiC and GaN components and energy storage to enable high-power AI data centers.

properties.table_content:
| Stage/Location   | Component/Function         | Voltage Transformation             | Key Materials/Description                                           |
|------------------|----------------------------|------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Infrastructure   | AC/DC Converter            | MV AC Grid Input to 800V DC Output | Utilizes SiC and High Power Modules                                 |
|                  | Long Duration Energy Storage | 800V DC Bus to V_bat             | Lithium-ion Batteries (Li-ion), requires SiC for DC/DC conversion   |
| Hall             | DC/DC Converter            | 800V DC Bus                        | Connects medium duration storage to the 800V bus                   |
|                  | Medium Duration Energy Storage | 800V DC Bus to V_bat             | Super Capacitors / New Battery Chemistry, requires SiC for DC/DC conversion |
| Row / IT Rack    | DC/DC Converter            | 800V DC Bus                        | Connects short duration storage to the 800V bus                    |
|                  | Short Duration Energy Storage | 800V DC Bus to V_bat             | Electrolytic Capacitors, requires SiC for DC/DC conversion          |
| Serverboard      | HV IBC (High Voltage IBC)  | 800V DC Input to 54V/12V DC Output | Employs GaN for efficient high-voltage conversion                   |
|                  | LV IBC (Low Voltage IBC)   | 54V DC Input to 12V/6V DC Output   | Uses GaN, Silicon (Si), and Control ICs                             |
|                  | VRM (Voltage Regulator Module)| 12V/6V DC Input to Core Voltage  | Employs Silicon (Si) and Control ICs for final power delivery       |
| System-wide      | Safety Breakers            | Across 800V DC Bus                 | Ensures system safety at various stages                             |
properties.key_insight: The Future GW-scale data center architecture progressively steps down voltage from an MV AC grid to core levels (800V DC→54V→12V/6V), integrating SiC and GaN materials with distributed energy storage at each stage.

source.name: Table T1 – Future GW-scale data center architecture
source.brief: Hierarchical data center power delivery architecture featuring voltage step-down and advanced materials.
source.description: Outlines multi-stage power conversion from MV AC to serverboard core, leveraging SiC and GaN components and energy storage to enable high-power AI data centers.

properties.table_content:
| Stage/Location   | Component/Function         | Voltage Transformation             | Key Materials/Description                                           |
|------------------|----------------------------|------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Infrastructure   | AC/DC Converter            | MV AC Grid Input to 800V DC Output | Utilizes SiC and High Power Modules                                 |
|                  | Long Duration Energy Storage | 800V DC Bus to V_bat             | Lithium-ion Batteries (Li-ion), requires SiC for DC/DC conversion   |
| Hall             | DC/DC Converter            | 800V DC Bus                        | Connects medium duration storage to the 800V bus                   |
|                  | Medium Duration Energy Storage | 800V DC Bus to V_bat             | Super Capacitors / New Battery Chemistry, requires SiC for DC/DC conversion |
| Row / IT Rack    | DC/DC Converter            | 800V DC Bus                        | Connects short duration storage to the 800V bus                    |
|                  | Short Duration Energy Storage | 800V DC Bus to V_bat             | Electrolytic Capacitors, requires SiC for DC/DC conversion          |
| Serverboard      | HV IBC (High Voltage IBC)  | 800V DC Input to 54V/12V DC Output | Employs GaN for efficient high-voltage conversion                   |
|                  | LV IBC (Low Voltage IBC)   | 54V DC Input to 12V/6V DC Output   | Uses GaN, Silicon (Si), and Control ICs                             |
|                  | VRM (Voltage Regulator Module)| 12V/6V DC Input to Core Voltage  | Employs Silicon (Si) and Control ICs for final power delivery       |
| System-wide      | Safety Breakers            | Across 800V DC Bus                 | Ensures system safety at various stages                             |
properties.key_insight: The Future GW-scale data center architecture progressively steps down voltage from an MV AC grid to core levels (800V DC→54V→12V/6V), integrating SiC and GaN materials with distributed energy storage at each stage.

target.name: Table T1 – WULF Compute Core Business Model Comparison
target.brief: Comparison of WULF Compute's three business models
target.description: Details operational and financial metrics for CSP, Colocation, and Build to Suit models

properties.table_content:
| Metric | Cloud Service Provider (CSP) | Colocation - Whitespace & Rack Ready | Build to Suit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Description | Shell data center and GPU clusters; space, power, cooling, fiber/internet, security, compute, storage and environment. | Shell data center; lease rack ready whitespace including redundant power, cooling, fiber/internet, and security | Data center built to spec; lease space, redundant power, cooling, fiber/internet, and security |
| Customer | Multiple - Managed through cloud partner | Multiple - Enterprise and well funded startups | Single - Hyperscaler |
| Contract Size | 0.1 - 50 MW | 0.5 - 100 MW+ | 100+ MW |
| Contract Term | 1 - 36 months | 5 - 15 years | 15+ years with renewals |
| O&M | WULF managed | WULF managed | Tenant managed |
| Build Cost per MW | $27 - 30 million (1) | $6 - 8 million (1) | $2 - 4 million (4) |
| Financing | Equity & Debt | Equity (initially) | Highly Bankable |
| Revenue per MW | $11 - 18 million (2) | $1.3 - 1.8 million (3) | $0.2 - 0.5 million |
| Margins | 70 - 80% | 65 - 75% | 90% + |
| Valuation Range | 7-12x EBITDA | 10-15x EBITDA | 15-20x EBITDA |
properties.key_insight: The 'Build to Suit' model delivers lower build costs per MW ($2-4M), the highest margins (90%+), and premium valuations (15-20x EBITDA).

| 2012 | $(800) to +700 | Mixed flows |
| 2013 | $(800) to +700 | Mixed flows |
| 2014 | $(800) to +1,200 | Notable positive spikes |

| 2018 | $(2,000) to +1,000 | Wider fluctuations, strong positive flows |
| 2019 | $(1,500) to +1,000 | Mixed flows |
| 2020 | $(1,500) to +800 | Mixed flows, negative during market downturn |
| 2021 | $(2,000) to +1,200 | Strong positive and negative swings |
| 2022 | $(2,000) to +1,600 | Significant positive peaks |
| 2023 | $(1,500) to +800 | Mixed flows |
| 2024 | $(1,500) to +1,000 | Mixed flows |

target.name: Table T1 – Data Center Financing Needs and Funding Breakdown
target.brief: Projected data center financing needs and funding sources through 2028
target.description: Lists global capex, financing gap, and breakdown of funding mechanisms

properties.table_content:
| Financial Segment / Need           | Value ($Billion) | Timeframe / Scope      | Details / Source                                     |
|------------------------------------|------------------|------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| Global Data Center Capex (Total)   | 2,900            | Through 2028           | For build and hardware costs                         |
| Hyperscaler Capex (Covered)        | 1,400            |                        | Funded by internal cash flows                        |
| Estimated Financing Gap            | 1,500            | Medium-term            | Needs external capital to fill                       |
| Private Credit Opportunity         | 800+             | Through 2028           | Led by Asset-Based Finance (ABF)                     |
| Incremental IG Tech Bond Supply    | 200              | Through 2028           | Expected corporate bond issuance                     |
| Data Center Securitized Credit     | 150              | Through 2028           | Projected ABS/CMBS issuance                          |
| US Securitized Issuance (Current)  | ~50              | To date                | Backed by ~10% of US data center capacity            |
| US Securitization Rate (Projected) | 25%              | By 2028                | Of new GWs in US securitized market                  |
properties.key_insight: Projected $2.9tr global data center capex through 2028 creates a $1.5tr financing gap to be filled by private credit, bonds, and securitization.

source.name: Table T1 – WULF Compute Core Business Model Comparison
source.brief: Comparison of WULF Compute's three business models
source.description: Details operational and financial metrics for CSP, Colocation, and Build to Suit models

properties.table_content:
| Metric | Cloud Service Provider (CSP) | Colocation - Whitespace & Rack Ready | Build to Suit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Description | Shell data center and GPU clusters; space, power, cooling, fiber/internet, security, compute, storage and environment. | Shell data center; lease rack ready whitespace including redundant power, cooling, fiber/internet, and security | Data center built to spec; lease space, redundant power, cooling, fiber/internet, and security |
| Customer | Multiple - Managed through cloud partner | Multiple - Enterprise and well funded startups | Single - Hyperscaler |
| Contract Size | 0.1 - 50 MW | 0.5 - 100 MW+ | 100+ MW |
| Contract Term | 1 - 36 months | 5 - 15 years | 15+ years with renewals |
| O&M | WULF managed | WULF managed | Tenant managed |
| Build Cost per MW | $27 - 30 million (1) | $6 - 8 million (1) | $2 - 4 million (4) |
| Financing | Equity & Debt | Equity (initially) | Highly Bankable |
| Revenue per MW | $11 - 18 million (2) | $1.3 - 1.8 million (3) | $0.2 - 0.5 million |
| Margins | 70 - 80% | 65 - 75% | 90% + |
| Valuation Range | 7-12x EBITDA | 10-15x EBITDA | 15-20x EBITDA |
properties.key_insight: The 'Build to Suit' model delivers lower build costs per MW ($2-4M), the highest margins (90%+), and premium valuations (15-20x EBITDA).

| Data Center Securitized Credit     | 150              | Through 2028           | Projected ABS/CMBS issuance                          |

| Year | Approx. Two-Week Net Flow Range ($mn) | Observation |
|---|---|---|
| 2008 | $(1,000) to +500 | Mixed flows, fluctuating around zero |

| 2011 | $(800) to +600 | Mixed flows |
| 2012 | $(800) to +700 | Mixed flows |
| 2013 | $(800) to +700 | Mixed flows |

properties.table_content:
| Financial Segment / Need           | Value ($Billion) | Timeframe / Scope      | Details / Source                                     |
|------------------------------------|------------------|------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| Global Data Center Capex (Total)   | 2,900            | Through 2028           | For build and hardware costs                         |
